extracted.intended_audience: readers and practitioners interested in stage magic, performance craft, and 19th-century theatrical memoirs
extracted.subtask_description: Anecdotal/practical guidance embedded in memoir prose about producing and managing 19th-century stage-magic performances (timing, misdirection, audience-handling, prop preparation, assistant coordination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise timing and punctuality
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of exactness in timing for entrances, intermissions, and transitions; the King even admonishes 'je vous recommande l'exactitude.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan and calculate intervals between sessions carefully; prepare contingencies for delays (e.g., delegate tasks while regaining breath) and avoid long gaps (an entr'acte of twenty minutes is excessive). Timing affects audience patience and the reception of subsequent effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid recovery and composed stage presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to regain composure after fatigue or anxiety and to present the stereotyped smile and confident demeanor despite internal stress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short breathing/rest pauses, delegate immediate actions to an assistant to buy time, and rehearse maintaining a calm, engaging appearance so the audience relaxes and the performance resumes smoothly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of an assistant (especially a child) to disarm the audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Deploy a sympathetic assistant to perform simple preparations onstage (tabouret, ardoise, cartes, bandeau) and to charm or distract the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce the assistant visibly and let them perform small, credible tasks to occupy attention, humanize the act, and defuse impatience or hostility from the crowd.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secret communication and coordinated signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliance on an 'insaisissable' material communication between performer and assistant (the 'procédé des deux pensées simultanées') to coordinate revelations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop robust, covert signaling systems and rehearsed correspondences that allow the assistant to supply specific technical names, values, or descriptions on cue without obvious prompting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensive reference knowledge and memory
rubrics_metrics.description: Mastery of factual knowledge (coin types and dates, heraldic blazons, names of surgical instruments, mineralogy, languages' scripts) to make identifications authoritative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build and memorize reference information so that when an object is 'read' you can state precise technical details (e.g., coin issuer and year) to convince skeptical audiences; use specialists' collections for study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secret physical techniques for inspecting sealed items
rubrics_metrics.description: Manual sleight and concealed manipulation (e.g., opening boxes, unsealing packages, opening watches single-handed) to surreptitiously inspect objects presented as sealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice dexterity techniques (keeping one thumbnail long and sharp, single-hand watch opening) so inspection leaves no perceptible trace; rehearse to perform these actions without attracting attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellent observational acuity and rapid scanning
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing the ability to rapidly note and recall visible details in an environment (bookshelf titles, jewelry, apartment contents) to recreate or 'read' them later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train vision and memory to perform quick, unobtrusive surveys of a room or person; use pre-performance walks or glances to gather material the assistant will later 'divine.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Misdirection and conversational tactics to buy time
rubrics_metrics.description: Using dialogue, feigned embarrassment, or extended conversation to distract challengers while the performer deduces or prepares the trick (e.g., feigning inability to see a seat number to deduce it by logic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft plausible verbal responses that lower an adversary's guard and permit the performer to compute or obtain needed information; elongate exchanges strategically to create opportunities for secret work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and prepare for challengers' stunt items
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect incrédules to bring difficult or sealed objects (antique medals, minerals, foreign-script books, sealed packets) and prepare methods to handle them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a repertoire of inspection techniques and fallback routines for many object types; keep tools and practiced motions ready to neutralize attempts to embarrass the act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of environmental manipulation and accomplices
rubrics_metrics.description: Manipulating surroundings or engaging accomplices (e.g., raising temperature to make a hat be removed) to expose concealed features for observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate discreetly with venue staff to create benign environmental changes or small staged distractions that reveal needed visual information; ensure staff understand timing and desired effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor effects to the occasion and verify credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Design special tricks for distinguished audiences (royalty) and arrange independent checks (e.g., having persons guard the chosen place) to heighten perceived impossibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose bespoke effects that suit the venue and audience prestige; encourage genuine verification measures so success appears less staged and more astonishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stagecraft and elegant prop arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: Attention to the visual presentation of instruments and symmetry on stage to contribute to an elegant and credible appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange tables and apparatus symmetrically and attractively; small details of mise-en-scène enhance perceived professionalism and audience receptivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience management and crowd-control policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical policies for ticketing, admission, and dealing with overcrowding or invasion of the theatre (posting notices, closing doors, offering refunds, or giving a gratis performance to mollify crowds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish clear ticketing rules and staff protocols for handling unruly groups; consider humane, reputation-preserving responses (free performance, gifts, later refunds) rather than force or police intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generosity and public-relations as mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Using gifts, free performances, and courteous behavior toward the audience to turn inconveniences into favorable publicity and prolong vogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When incidents occur, be lavish and gracious (distribute presents, forgive unpaid seats) to convert potential scandal into goodwill and increased reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical problem-solving and improvisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Quick, pragmatic decisions in the face of unexpected events (e.g., appointing a gratis show, changing seat configuration to accommodate special booking requests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be ready to improvise solutions—alter seating, reassign benches, or adjust program flow—so operations continue and relationships (with patrons, critics) are preserved.
